newsitem.title: USA: US cash distillates jump, gasoline stable on APIs.
newsitem.headline: US cash distillates jump, gasoline stable on APIs.

text.p: U.S. late cash distillates jumped sharply but gasoline remained stable in after-hours ACCESS trade following API data showing a slim distillate build and moderate gasoline build for the prior week.
But differentials were narrowly mixed, as in previous sessions during the past week, as many players remained on the sidelines amid continuing developments in Iraq.

Heating oil gained about one cent, with ACCESS futures adding another 0.60 cent to a 0.30-cent gain scored in earlier NYMEX trade. The price rise was spurred by API data showing a mere 235,000-barrel distillate build for the week ending Sept. 13, players said.
The poor distillate build put total U.S. stocks at 21.5 million barrels below last year, according to the API data.
"Heat is going to be a real star if we get any cold weather," one Midcontinent trader said, noting U.S. distillate stocks now stand about 16 percent below last year.
Gasoline futures rose about 0.25 cent a gallon in ACCESS trade, more than offsetting a 0.13-cent decline in earlier NYMEX activity, traders said.
The API report showed total U.S. gasoline stocks rising 434,000 barrels, to about 2.9 million below last year.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
